svg.text: Subquery vs CTE vs EXISTS – Visual Guide
SQL · S02 · Name the step; EXISTS for “any”; CTE is not a hint
A CTE names a step. EXISTS stops at the first match.
Filter, name the aggregate, then join.
A CTE can feed the outer query and a second consumer.
IN + DISTINCT builds a list. EXISTS can stop early.

text.tspan: Builds a list; does not stop early

svg.text: WITH LatestBeat, then LEFT JOIN — still check the plan.
CTE is a name, not a hint
LEFT JOIN LatestBeat b ON b.DeviceId = d.Id;
Named step, then join — not automatically faster.
Any() is EXISTS. A second IQueryable is a CTE.

text.tspan: CTE for two or three named steps
EXISTS when you only need “any row”
Say the optimizer may inline the CTE
